speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You have presented with gait and limb ataxia; to begin our evaluation, can you describe exactly when these symptoms started and if they have been progressively worsening? Additionally, what specific significant medical conditions or surgeries are in your history?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the sensation of looking "drunk" while walking and right-sided clumsiness suggests cerebellar involvement. To narrow this down, is there a specific family member who died young from a similar condition, or do you experience other neurological issues like slurred speech or double vision? Also, have you had any recent head trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy, likely precipitated by Crohn's disease.

I have determined the diagnosis based on your history of PML risk factors (natalizumab use for Crohn's) and the presentation of cerebellar ataxia. The next logical step is to confirm this with imaging. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain (without contrast).
